artists.biography: Best known as the action hero behind cinema's Die Hard series, Bruce Willis became a twice-over recording artist during the late '80s. His debut album, The Return of Bruno, became a surprise seller after the single "Respect Yourself" hit the Top Five in early 1987. Willis had two other modest hits, and recorded another LP two years later, but has remained outside music for the most part -- performing only occasionally to inaugurate several Planet Hollywood restaurants.
artists.name: Bruce Willis

Bruce Willis.biography: Best known as the action hero behind cinema's Die Hard series, Bruce Willis became a twice-over recording artist during the late '80s. His debut album, The Return of Bruno, became a surprise seller after the single "Respect Yourself" hit the Top Five in early 1987. Willis had two other modest hits, and recorded another LP two years later, but has remained outside music for the most part -- performing only occasionally to inaugurate several Planet Hollywood restaurants.

perplexity.description:
The Return of Bruno is Bruce Willis's debut studio album, released in January 1987 on Motown Records. The record showcases an eclectic blend of R&B, funk, and soul, featuring Willis performing over arrangements that draw from classic soul and contemporary funk styles. The album benefits from accomplished session musicians and vocalists, including Booker T. Jones, The Pointer Sisters, and The Temptations, who provide backing vocals and instrumental support across the ten-track collection.

The album functions as a companion piece to an HBO television special of the same name that aired shortly after its release, positioning Willis's musical venture as part of a broader multimedia project. While Willis was primarily known as an actor at the time, the album represents an early attempt by a Hollywood figure to establish credibility in the music industry during the 1980s. The production quality is professional, with the album mastered at Bernie Grundman Mastering, reflecting a serious investment in the project's sonic presentation.

The album received modest critical attention, with an IMDb rating of 5.9/10 for the accompanying television special suggesting lukewarm reception. Despite the involvement of respected session musicians and the Motown label's prestige, the album did not achieve significant commercial success, remaining largely a curiosity in Willis's career. A reissue was later distributed by Razor & Tie in 1997, though the original 1987 release remains the definitive version of this early foray into music by the actor.
